data.function: uWS::HttpParser::consumePostPadded (fallback branch); underflowing arithmetic at lines 336-337, enabled by fenceAndConsumePostPadded proxy handling at lines 196-219 and 276-284
data.bug_class: unsigned integer underflow (consumed.first - had) causing out-of-bounds pointer arithmetic -> heap-buffer-overflow read/write (observed as SEGV read before the allocation)
data.rationale:
Reachability: fuzz target HttpWithProxy (fuzzing/Http.cpp, -DUWS_WITH_PROXY) splits input into chunks and feeds each to HttpParser::consumePostPadded. Chunk 1 = 'GET /hi HTTP/1.1

' + a complete 16-byte PROXY v2 frame (

\x00
QUIT
, ver_cmd 0x21, fam 0, len 0) + 'GET /hi HTTP

' + filler. In fenceAndConsumePostPadded the HTTP request is consumed, then the loop's getHeaders cannot parse the data beginning with the PROXY frame's leading '

' (returns 0 at i==0), so the entire remainder (frame + a COMPLETE request + filler) is appended to the fallback buffer while the proxy parser itself did not consume it. On the next chunk, the fallback path re-parses: ProxyParser now consumes the frame (offset 16) and getHeaders parses the complete request that lies entirely INSIDE the old fallback, so consumed.first (36) < had (fallback length). The code's own comment (lines 332-334) assumes 'we consumed everything in fallback buffer'; the guard at lines 280-282 only catches consumedProxyParser==consumedTotal and does not cover this case. Thus 'consumed.first - had' underflows: data is moved backwards before the chunk start and length is inflated. The subsequent ProxyParser::parse memcmp (ProxyParser.h:103) on the corrupted data pointer reads before the 512KB makePadded heap allocation -> ASAN error (heap out-of-bounds read, reported as SEGV due to secondary-allocator guard pages). Verified empirically with a crafted 322-byte input against the ASAN build.
